hook.text: Your API allows 10 requests a minute for each key.
hook.say: Your A P I allows ten requests a minute for each key.

hook.text: How does the server count them?
The simplest way is a fixed window.

count.text: Each minute gets one counter in Redis.
Every request adds one to it.
Request 11 finds 10 already there, and gets refused with 429.
count.say: Request eleven finds ten already there, and gets refused with four twenty-nine.

edge.text: But watch the edge of a minute.

edge.say: Ten requests at fifty-five seconds. All allowed.

edge.text: A new minute starts, with a new counter at zero.

edge.say: Ten more at one minute and five seconds. All allowed too.
That's twenty requests in ten seconds.

takeaway.text: Fixed windows are cheap: one number and one command.
Use them when a short burst at the edge is fine.
Next: the sliding window log fixes the edge.

cta.text: Try it in Structura: send 10 at 55 seconds, then 10 at 65.
cta.say: Try it in Structura: send ten at fifty-five seconds, then ten at sixty-five.
